game.summary: Wired the objective ledger into MatchRoom (apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts, new objectives.ts). A slice ledger is seeded from the room's private randomness. Its sources are 2 per island at the island's docks, and all are unlocked until the ruins are wired. Holding E while moored collects the island's first eligible source, or else claims a cached rubbing; release, cast-off, reservation or disconnect resets the hold, and starting one ends protection via protectionEndedBy. Duels: reserveDuel and reportDuelResult are called, and 'settled' goes to the encounter rules only once the ledger settles (choose-theft message, protocol v6, zod-validated, winner only; the default applies at the deadline). The world tick drives section 12: disconnectPlayer at the drop, a 10 s duel absence counted in ticks, expireReservation at the deadline into a cache at the rules' respawn dock, and every other leave (including Colyseus' 70 s outer bound) is a quitPlayer into a cache at the nearest dock by sea. checkLedger plus a room invariant (no ship without a ledger player and vice versa) run every tick in development and tests; production turns them off. Hidden info: gold, rubbings, holds and theft options are in the player's own status only; island and cache types only while moored there; contentless cache markers within sight; the grapple defenderId is blanked through a twin entry. Web: purse panel (gold, rubbings, settlement notice, theft choice on keys 1/2 or a click), HUD island/cache/hold progress/result lines, cache chests. Marker drawing moved to a Phaser-free markers.ts with a unit test. The match game was switched to Phaser.CANVAS after the measured tick p95 failed with AUTO (135 ms; 8.5/8.9 ms with canvas). Tests: new integration files rubbings/rubbingsExpiry/rubbingsOuterBound (one tuning per file, since there is one matchmaker per process); seaDuel updates (moving ship stops on reservation, ready-timeout cancel at 200 ticks, tick-counted absence); a real draw moving nothing in seaDuelHarness; web and server unit tests; the theft-loop Playwright scenario; sea-duel taps keys and asserts the tick p95. Integration budget: test-only overrides first (startGameServer matchTuning, duelReconnectSeconds), then fork parallelism (3 workers) with the harness files in a serial second group. Before: 201.65 s (old 55-test suite). Overrides only, serial, 73 tests: 263.64 s. Final: 117.17 s with the harness green. Checks actually run in this worktree: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (900 pass), npm run test:integration (73 pass, 117.17 s), npm run build (pass, smoke test extended), and the full Playwright suite with a JSON report: 8/8 pass, check-report ok for all 8 scenarios. Docs updated: architecture.md, duel.md, encounters.md, objectives.md and README.md.
open_assumptions: policy.json's theft-loop description says 'held attack keys', but the task says duel buttons fire on the press, so the scenario taps U repeatedly and its title says 'taps attack keys'. policy.json is not an owned path, so its wording is unchanged.

'The respawn dock the encounter rules would choose' for an expiry is computed with seaModeRules.respawnPoint from the expiring ship's current position (or its pending respawn position), with the other ships not waiting to respawn as opponents.
A quitter's 'nearest dock by sea' is measured from the ship's current tile (for a fighter, where its ship was reserved) with content's seaPathCosts, ties to the lower dock id.
Cache claims set protectionEndedBy 'collection', because the encounter rules only accept 'claim' (the treasure claim) or 'collection'.

The integration project runs 3 fork workers, with maxConcurrency 20 for concurrent tests. The netcode harness files (duelHarness, seaDuelHarness, devLatency) run afterwards as a separate serial project, and npm run test:integration runs both projects.
The standalone DuelRoom gets a test-only reconnection window (duelReconnectSeconds, 6 s in duel.test.ts); production keeps DUEL_RECONNECT_SECONDS.
